title: An eval route whose provider cannot serve the role silently falls through to another provider
summary: eval.call_route -> delegate(provider=X) uses the analyst role. router.select treats an unusable override (e.g. an HTTP endpoint registered with roles ['inline']) as 'override provider X ignored' and routes the case to the cheapest usable provider instead. The EVR row keeps the requested route spec as 'ref' but records the provider that actually answered, so a reader comparing refs could attribute another model's accuracy to the candidate. The fall-through is intentional for coding runs (overrides are advisory there), but for measurement it is an attribution error. Mitigated outside the protected harness: evalqueue refuses candidates lacking the analyst role and marks a run invalid when the recorded provider differs from the requested one; model-add gained --roles. A harness-level fix (fail the route when its override is not honoured) needs an operator grant because eval.py is a protected control-plane path (IMP-0017).

provenance.session: ORCH-0031 -> ORCH-0032 (code reading while building the eval-queue runner)
